title: Dental Unit Water Failed Standards More Often at Outlets Than at the Inlet in China Study
html:
Water from dental unit equipment outlets met microbiological standards significantly less often than water entering the units, according to a cross-sectional study of 67 medical institutions in Lianyungang, China, published Nov. 23 in Scientific Reports.

Of 620 dental unit waterline samples, 458 (73.87%) met the applicable water quality standard. Inlet water had the highest compliance at 91.59%. After adjustment for clustering of samples within institutions, compliance at every equipment outlet tested, including the scaler connecting tube, three-way syringe, cup filler, and handpiece connecting tube, remained significantly lower than at the inlet.

Compliance also varied by institution level, from 85.25% at tertiary hospitals to 69.20% at ungraded institutions. Public and private institutions did not differ significantly (76.03% vs. 71.95%).

The study was designed to compare traditional Chinese medicine hospitals with general and specialized stomatology hospitals. General hospitals had the highest sample compliance at 76.70%, followed by stomatology hospitals at 73.79% and the four traditional Chinese medicine hospitals at 50.00%. That gap was not statistically significant after accounting for clustering, and compliance within individual traditional Chinese medicine hospitals ranged from 0% to 100%. One of those hospitals had multiple samples positive for Escherichia coli.

Institutions were selected by stratified random sampling, and researchers combined a questionnaire survey with bacterial culture of water samples.

The study was conducted by Jing Li of the Lianyungang Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Han Qi of Lianyungang Second People’s Hospital, and Dongsheng Zhu of Lianyungang First People’s Hospital. The authors reported no funding and no competing interests.

The authors described the findings as exploratory and said differences between hospital types require validation in larger multicenter studies.

Sources:
Scientific Reports, “A multicenter cross-sectional study on the disparity of dental unit waterline contamination between traditional Chinese medicine and general hospitals,” Nov. 23, 2026: nature.com/articles/s41598-026-81737-x
